proposal_kernel_provenance.rule: the proposal names the kernel it was authored on; a later authorized kernel changes that field only — tolerated when it is the one differing path and the committed value is the accepted candidate's kernel

06_or_iface_1.ruling: APPROVED WITH SCOPE LIMITATION: Ledger(path) with apply_batch, snapshot, verify and operation stimuli as JSON arrays, for the exact PLAN-V2.2 BehaviorContracts of the LedgerLock Cycle-2 DEVELOPMENT_REGRESSION workload
06_or_iface_1.semantics: an OPERATIONAL CONTRACT BINDING for this qualification/regression workload; NOT a statement that the frozen prose requirements mandate this Python API shape; not framework-wide; not evidence that arbitrary conforming LedgerLock implementations must expose it; its authority is only the exact human-approved contract hashes

interface_binding_as_proposed.binding: a Ledger is constructed with its ledger file path, Ledger(<path>), and offers apply_batch(ops), snapshot() and verify() as methods; ops are (op, key, value, rid, ts) delivered as 5-element JSON arrays (a contract stimulus is JSON data)
interface_binding_as_proposed.source: §5 names apply_batch(ops) and its tuple shape, §6 snapshot(), §3.4 verify from the library, §12 'the configured ledger path', §13 the class Ledger
interface_binding_as_proposed.gap: the requirements do not say how a Ledger is bound to its path, nor that an implementation must accept arrays where they say tuples; every process_effect spec depends on this binding (the reference and PLAN-V2.1 read it the same way) — open normative gap OG-IB-LEDGER

OR-IFACE-2.ruling: APPROVED WITH SCOPE LIMITATION: a delete's value slot is null; ts is an integer the caller supplies — the canonical test stimulus representation of the exact approved benchmark contracts
OR-IFACE-2.semantics: a stimulus convention of the approved benchmark contracts; no broader requirement claim; no new framework semantics

interface_binding_as_proposed.binding: a delete element carries null in its value slot; ts is an integer the caller supplies
interface_binding_as_proposed.source: §5 gives every element the shape (op, key, value, rid, ts); §3.2 gives a delete line no value
interface_binding_as_proposed.gap: the requirements do not say what a delete's value slot holds

binding.ruling: APPROVED WITH SCOPE LIMITATION: an existing zero-byte ledger file is a fresh ledger state — the canonical initial-state interpretation of the exact approved benchmark contracts
binding.semantics: binds the exact approved contract set; not framework-wide; no generalization claim; the frozen requirements document is not altered

interface_binding_as_proposed.binding: a zero-byte file is a fresh, empty ledger (a valid chain of no lines)
interface_binding_as_proposed.source: §14 item 1 'a fresh ledger'; §3.3 (ok when every line verifies)
interface_binding_as_proposed.gap: a 'fresh ledger' could also be a path that does not exist yet, which §9 makes an I/O error (RISK-4); the specs on an empty ledger (S-5-a, S-6-d, S-7-d, S-9-a, S-9-c, S-9-e) read it as a zero-byte file

prose_vs_content.reading: the zero-byte ruling binds the contracts whose content holds a zero-byte ledger file; a process_effect contract that constructs Ledger(path) over a path with no file starts fresh under OR-IFACE-1's Ledger(path) binding, as its exact approved hash encodes; the prose inaccuracy is disclosed, no contract changes

corrected_statement: S-5-a does NOT rely on the zero-byte-existing-file interpretation (OR-IFACE-3): its stimulus holds no ledger file at all; its scenario constructs Ledger(<ws>/l.jsonl) over a path with no file, as its exact approved contract hash encodes
the OR-IFACE-3 ruling applies only where the stimulus actually contains an existing zero-byte ledger: S-6-d, S-7-d, S-9-a, S-9-c, S-9-e
no BehaviorContract changes; no ProductProofSpec changes; no semantic_hash changes; no plan_hash change; no falsifiability evidence invalidated

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: hash = SHA-256(prev_hash || '|' || canonical_bytes), hash fields emptied
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: the canonical bytes encoding is not fixed: no harness can recompute a hash value independently; the product's own consistency is observed through its verify (S-3.2-a, S-3.3-*)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: first prev_hash is 'GENESIS' or 64 zeros, an implementation choice, documented and constant
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: a disjunctive expected value: every file shape compares one value; fixing one form would enforce a stronger property than the requirement (OD-STRONGER)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: ok=False and first_bad_index=<i> on the first violation
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: the verdict's representation is open (the CLI exposes the exit code only); no class reads one field of an arbitrary returned object; a fixed-shape comparison would prescribe a representation (OD-02-01-4)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: the second call MUST return the same result
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: the result's representation is open; the only comparator of two results needs a JSON form, which would prescribe one (OD-RETURN)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: or return an error result depending on CLI surface (exit 4, §9)
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: the only mutating CLI invocation is `apply --batch <file>`, whose file shape the requirements do not fix (OD-BATCH)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: ... returning the same result as the delete

09_unsupported_clauses.reason: the requirements define no lock and nothing observable depends on one

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: apply_batch writes all lines to a sibling temp file, fsyncs it, renames it over the path
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: the mechanism is not observable by any class (no step traces the subject's own files)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: a crash at any point leaves the full batch or the pre-batch bytes, never a partial batch
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: a fault step makes the faulted call either return (call) or raise (expect_raises); the requirements fix neither, only the post-crash state, and a fault the implementation does not use (os.replace vs os.rename) never fires (OD-03-01-5)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: the CLI `apply --batch <file>` performs the same atomic operation
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: the batch-file shape is not fixed (OD-BATCH); the file-absent I/O error is measured (S-9-e)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: sorted by NFC key in UTF-8 byte order; a JSON document
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: the document's layout and representation are open: its content and key order are observable only through bytes or a representation no requirement fixes

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: the CLI `snapshot --out <file>` writes this same document
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: no class compares a written file with a library value, and the file's bytes are layout-open

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: no other content may be modified
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: the preserved lines were written by the product: their bytes are unknown to the harness (S-7-a measures that they remain)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: after a successful append the bytes are durably on disk (fsync) before return
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: durability is not observable from outside the process (the reference fixture treats R-8 as static)

09_unsupported_clauses.clause: no opening of files outside the ledger, batch and snapshot paths
09_unsupported_clauses.reason: no class observes which files a subject opens

10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-1: a key with a committed put can never be deleted or changed (a same-rid delete replays, another rid conflicts): R-6's 'unless tombstoned by a later delete' is unreachable for a put key; tombstones exist only as a first mutation
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-2: R-4.5 'replays of either MUST NOT conflict' holds only for the committed put (S-4.5-b); the refused delete replayed is again another rid (R-4.3)
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-3: replay scope rid alone or rid+key: no spec reuses a rid across keys
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-4: 'verify: any other exit code is a bug' vs 2 and 3; 'fresh ledger' consistent only as an existing empty file (IB-EMPTY)
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-5: 'any modification detected' vs hashing canonical bytes: only semantic edits are testable (S-3.3-* edit value, op, hash, prev_hash)
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-6: the GENESIS form is both 'the literal' and an implementation choice (R-3.2/4 UNSUPPORTED)
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-7: §12 file confinement vs §5's sibling temp file (R-12/2 UNSUPPORTED)
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-9: a newline-terminated corrupt last line is neither truncated nor 'in the middle' (AC-STORY-03-02-4 UNSUPPORTED)
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-10: conflicts and replays between elements of one batch: R-4.3 judges against committed mutations (S-5-a conflicts against a committed line)
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-11: §10's allowed set omits __future__ (which §10 requires) and the package's own modules: S-10-a admits both
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-12: §3.2's line shapes omit hash and prev_hash, which every line carries
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-13: module functions vs methods; append/put/delete signatures and ts provenance open (IB-LEDGER, IB-ELEMENTS)
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-14: durability, crash atomicity, file confinement and the interpreter version are outside every probe
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-15: '0 — success (append …)' names a CLI append no clause specifies
10_requirement_ambiguities.RISK-16: 'no third-party imports succeed at runtime' reads as an environment property (R-14 item 6 mapped to S-10-a)
